beats.title: Introducing a Pluggable Recording Architecture
beats.body: A contributor proposed a base abstraction layer for recording controllers, enabling users to swap in alternative muxing backends beyond the built-in default. The goal was extensibility: third-party or custom recording implementations could be plugged in without modifying core library code.

beats.title: Where Should Community-Built Implementations Live?
beats.body: Once the abstraction was merged, concrete alternative implementations emerged. The question became: should the maintainer host these community-built controllers in the main project's ecosystem, or should ownership and hosting remain with the original contributor in a separate repository?

beats.title: Position A — FunnyDevs
beats.body: The contributor offered their implementations to the broader community and signaled openness to the maintainer deciding how to host them, implicitly suggesting the maintainer could create a dedicated companion repository similar to existing satellite projects.
beats.author: FunnyDevs

beats.title: Position B — pedroSG94
beats.body: The maintainer favored forking rather than re-hosting, reasoning that the code belongs to its author and should remain under their stewardship. The maintainer committed to referencing the external repository in documentation rather than absorbing it into the project.
beats.author: pedroSG94

beats.question: When a community member contributes implementations built on your abstraction, should a maintainer host them centrally or keep them in the contributor's own repository?
